question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ for $0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{5\pi }{4}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 3x-\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{7\pi }{4}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\frac{3\pi }{2}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & 3x & =2\pi +2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{2n\pi }{3} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+\frac{2n\pi }{3} \\ x & =\frac{\pi (4n+3)}{6} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{2(n+1)\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ (too big)

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\frac{\pi }{6}$ (too small) and $x=0.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\frac{2\pi }{3}.$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ are

$$
x=0,\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0+\frac{\pi }{2}=\frac{\pi }{2}.
$$
